title: JANUS Record Drift Observatory
purpose: Test whether previously recorded information remains byte-identical, semantically identical, and presentation-identical across later retrievals, while distinguishing legitimate revisions, rendering changes, storage corruption, identity changes, distributed divergence, and unexplained drift.

motivating_observation.example: A Dota match was remembered/observed as ending at 12:21, while a later replay/display appeared to show a different number.
motivating_observation.rule: The motivating observation is not evidence of data mutation and must not be used as a positive result. It only motivates prospective preregistered testing.

core_question: For a stable record identity R captured at T0, does the record retrieved at Tn differ from T0, and if so, at which layer did the divergence occur?

null_hypotheses.H0_immutable: For immutable controls, raw content and pinned identity remain unchanged across checks.
null_hypotheses.H0_live: For mutable/live records, any change is explainable by an explicit revision, version, branch movement, source update, timezone/rendering transformation, or identity change.
null_hypotheses.anomaly_candidate: Only a reproducible divergence that survives identity, raw-byte, timestamp, parser, cache, replica, revision-history, and local-storage checks may be labelled unexplained drift.

measurement_layers.note: Used only in addition to raw bytes, never instead of them. JSON key ordering/whitespace normalization must not hide raw-byte drift.

A_git_immutable.members: Files retrieved by immutable Git commit/blob identity from Hawkar-usls/janus-meta-registry.
A_git_immutable.failure_if: Pinned historical object content changes while the exact same object identity remains valid.

B_git_live.role: positive control for ordinary declared evolution
B_git_live.members: The same repository paths retrieved from moving branch main.
B_git_live.expected: May change when main advances; change must map to commit history.
B_git_live.failure_if: Live content differs without a resolvable commit/identity transition.

C_registry_artifacts.members: JANUS JSON artifacts, audit receipts, manifests, test results, and future finalized outputs.
C_registry_artifacts.rule: Every finalized result becomes a monitored subject at its first committed state.

D_test_results.members: Eye In The Sky and future experiment result JSON/CSV summaries.
D_test_results.rule: Results are evidence objects, not truth objects. Their raw bytes, semantics, and later interpretation are monitored separately.

E_journal_self_control.rule: Entry N cannot contain its own final hash. Instead entry N+1 records and verifies the committed identity/hash of entry N. This one-generation delay avoids a self-hash paradox.
E_journal_self_control.expected: Historical committed journal generations remain stable; the live journal may grow only through explicit new commits.

members.name: RFC 3339
members.purpose: Stable external text plus timestamp-format reference.

members.name: RFC 3161
members.purpose: External timestamping reference; future protocol may attach third-party timestamp receipts.

G_external_live.members: Authoritative sources with stable record identifiers and exposed revision/update metadata; sources are admitted individually before monitoring.
admission_requirements: no source selected because a drift was already noticed

drift_taxonomy.R0_STABLE: Identity, raw content, semantic fields, and declared presentation are unchanged within the comparison contract.
drift_taxonomy.R1_PRESENTATION_DRIFT: Raw/canonical/semantic record is stable but displayed representation changes.
drift_taxonomy.R2_INTERPRETATION_DRIFT: Raw record is stable but parser, schema, or derived semantic interpretation changes.
drift_taxonomy.R3_DECLARED_SOURCE_REVISION: Authoritative content changes with an explicit version/update/commit/revision trail.
drift_taxonomy.R4_UNDECLARED_REMOTE_CONTENT_DRIFT: Same stable remote identity returns different raw content without a discovered declared revision.
drift_taxonomy.R5_LOCAL_COPY_DRIFT: Local stored copy changes while independent pinned/remote controls remain stable.
drift_taxonomy.R6_DISTRIBUTED_DIVERGENCE: Replicas, caches, APIs, mirrors, or independent endpoints disagree for what is claimed to be the same record/version.
drift_taxonomy.R7_IDENTITY_DRIFT: A label/path/display name now resolves to a different underlying object; content changed because identity changed.
drift_taxonomy.R8_CLOCK_OR_TIMEZONE_DRIFT: Underlying instant is compatible but displayed/local time differs because of timezone, offset, locale, clock, or conversion rules.
drift_taxonomy.R9_JOURNAL_CHAIN_BREAK: A journal generation cannot validate the previous committed journal generation or expected previous-entry link.
drift_taxonomy.R10_UNEXPLAINED_CONFIRMED_DRIFT: A difference survives all registered identity, revision, raw-byte, presentation, parser, cache/replica, clock/timezone, and local-storage checks. This is an anomaly label, not a physical explanation.

capture_contract.timestamp_rule: Store UTC and numeric offset. Never store a naked local clock time as the only timestamp.
capture_contract.hash_rule: SHA-256 is the primary cross-system content hash; Git commit/blob identifiers are retained as additional repository-native identities.
capture_contract.canonicalization_rule: Canonicalized hashes are secondary diagnostics and must never replace the raw-byte hash.

journal_protocol.structure: append-only logical sequence represented by committed generation files/entries
journal_protocol.hash_chain: Each entry records the previous committed journal identity/hash. The next entry independently verifies it.
journal_protocol.journal_as_subject: Every committed journal generation is automatically admitted into the monitored set for the next generation.
journal_protocol.anti_rewrite_rule: Corrections are new entries; historical journal entries are not silently rewritten.
journal_protocol.chain_break_policy: A broken link is R9 until explained by an explicit repository history event.

recursive_evidence_rule.statement: The observatory's own outputs participate in later observatory checks.
examples: A test result JSON created today is hashed and becomes a subject tomorrow.
A journal entry created today is verified by the next journal entry.
A correction does not erase the earlier claim; both original and correction are separately preserved and monitored.
recursive_evidence_rule.guardrail: Self-reference increases provenance coverage but does not create independent evidence. Independent sources/replicas remain necessary for strong anomaly claims.

analysis_metrics.drift_rate_all: checks classified R1-R10 divided by all valid checks
analysis_metrics.raw_content_drift_rate: checks classified R3-R7 or R10 with confirmed raw difference divided by raw-checkable comparisons
analysis_metrics.unexplained_drift_rate: R10 divided by all valid checks

admission_gate_for_anomaly: T0 evidence predates discovery of drift
T0 and Tn raw evidence both available or content-addressed
local corruption checked against independent copy

relationship_to_eye_in_the_sky.extended_chain: EVENT -> RECORD(T0) -> TIME -> RECORD(Tn) -> OBSERVER -> INTERPRETATION
relationship_to_eye_in_the_sky.new_question: Does the record itself remain stable before observer interpretation is considered?
relationship_to_eye_in_the_sky.status: orthogonal extension; can use Eye In The Sky outputs as monitored records without inheriting its causal claims.

first_gate.name: T0 Genesis Baseline
requirements: register Eye In The Sky result artifacts
register the genesis journal itself for next-generation checking
register at least two external static controls
do not report positive drift at T0

next_version: v0.2 after repeated prospective captures and at least one independently classified ordinary revision case
